svg.aria-label: Fig 1. Arthai Health planned flow, drawn as nine stations on one bench. 1 claim builder and scrubber, 2 payer and clearinghouse mock, 3 remit posting, 4 triage (LLM by default, LAYA optional) with the CCI confidence gate, 5 review console and audit, 6 appeal writer, 7 voice agent, 8 AR follow-up, 9 eval and feedback loop. Chevrons on each track show the direction. Black tracks carry work from 1 to 2 to 3 to 4. Green track: the gate is sure, 4 to 6. Red track: the gate is not sure, 4 to the human queue in 5. Black tracks in front: 5 to 6 after a human decision, 6 to 5 for tier-2 approval, 5 to 7 after approval, and 7 to 8 with the call outcome. Dashed track: the call goes only to the mock payer in 2. Blue dotted track: reviewer edits go from 5 to 9, then recalibrate 4. Every station is planned. None is built.

svg.text: Synthetic data only. Every station is planned. None is built yet.
1 Claim builder and scrubber: builds the 837, runs NCCI and MUE edits
2 Payer and clearinghouse mock: our own fake payer, 835 and 277 out
3 Remit posting: reads the 835, finds each denied line
4 Triage + CCI gate: scorer (LLM or LAYA), conformal set picks the path
5 Review console + audit: human queue, approvals, audit trail
6 Appeal writer: Muse drafts, each statement cites a source
7 Voice agent: browser call to the mock payer rep
8 AR follow-up: ranks open claims for the next action
9 Eval and feedback loop: reviewer edits become eval cases
green: the gate is sure. 4 to 6.
red: the gate is not sure. 4 to the human queue in 5.
black: hand-off. 5 to 6 after a human decision.
black: 6 to 5 for tier-2 approval. 5 to 7 after approval.
dashed: the call goes only to our mock payer in 2.
blue dotted: reviewer edits go to 9, then recalibrate 4.
